chunks: Motor vs generator. The question: What is the difference between a motor and generator?
A motor and a generator are physically the same machine. The only difference is which way the energy flows. In a motor, electrical power goes in and the shaft turns.
In a generator, you turn the shaft and electrical power comes out.
Think of a bicycle with a hub dynamo. When you pedal, the wheel turns the dynamo and the light glows.
In principle, feeding the right kind of electricity into that same dynamo would push the wheel instead. Same machine, energy flowing the other way.
The analogy has one gap: real machines are often tuned for one job, so one direction works better than the other.
Motor mode at 500 rad/s: the supply (12 volts) exceeds the back-EMF (10 volts), so 1 amps flows into the machine.
Electrical input 12 watts = 2 watts heat in R + 10 watts mechanical output.
Motor: turns electrical power into mechanical power. Generator: turns mechanical power into electrical power. Back-EMF: the voltage a spinning motor generates against the supply.
It is speed times a motor constant: E equals K e omega , with speed omega in radians per second.
Regenerative braking: when the shaft is driven faster than the supply "expects", the motor feeds energy back.
No-load speed: the speed where back-EMF equals the supply, so no current flows.
Take a motor with K e equals 0. 02 volts per rad/s, on a 12 volts supply. Its no-load speed is 12 / 0. 02 = 600 rad/s.
At 300 rad/s, back-EMF is 6 volts, below the supply, so current flows in and it acts as a motor .
If you force the shaft to 700 rad/s, back-EMF is 14 volts, above the supply, so current flows out and it acts as a generator .
That is the whole idea: the same device switches roles at the speed where back-EMF equals the supply.
"A motor and a generator are the same machine with the energy flowing in opposite directions. A motor converts electrical power to mechanical: current in the field makes torque.
A generator converts mechanical to electrical: moving conductors in a field make a voltage. Inside every running motor there's also a back-EMF K e omega .
If you drive the shaft faster than V over K e , that back-EMF exceeds the supply, the current reverses and it regenerates. So the difference is just the sign of the power."
